task.description: Write test coverage for Letflow.Engine.cancel_instance/3 per lib/letflow/design/req052-instance-cancellation.md and REQ-052's 7 acceptance criteria (full text in this handoff's context.requirement_text reference, and in step-01-code-designer.json). Add tests to test/letflow/engine_test.exs (the existing file already covering create/2 and complete_task/3) following its established property-test conventions where state-machine-shaped, plus test/specs/REQ-052.md per your role's format. IMPORTANT (anti-pattern, see docs/anti-patterns.md): keep every combined describe+test name comfortably under 200 characters -- ExUnit hard-caps combined name length at 255 chars and this exact defect class has recurred 4 times on this project already. Note: test/letflow/parallel_approval_test.exs was deleted by ELIXIR-DEV alongside its now-deleted subject module -- do not attempt to re-migrate its coverage, that module no longer exists.
acceptance_criteria: cancelling an ACTIVE instance sets every open task to CANCELLED, appends exactly one INSTANCE_CANCELLED event, and sets the instance status to CANCELLED -- all committed together, verified by reading tasks, instance_projections and events back

cancelling an already-CANCELLED or already-COMPLETED instance returns a distinct conflict error and changes nothing; cancelling an ACTIVE instance with zero open tasks still appends INSTANCE_CANCELLED
after cancellation, a further append via REQ-025's append/1 is rejected by its existing active-instance guard -- demonstrated against the real event store rather than asserted from the code
a cancellation racing a task completion on the same instance resolves with exactly one winner and a distinct conflict error for the loser, run concurrently rather than sequentially

an instance cancelled via REQ-051's all-branches-cancelled join path and one cancelled by a direct cancel_instance call reach the same persisted state (status, task statuses, appended event), compared explicitly
the moduledoc names the SCH-03 timer-cancellation hook (S6) and the in-flight SERVICE_TASK abandonment hook (REQ-056) as explicitly out of scope, rather than implying EE-08 is fully covered

the moduledoc states concretely whether lib/letflow/parallel_approval.ex and Letflow.ApprovalSupervisor are deleted or retained-with-a-stated-reason, and mix test passes with the actual output quoted after the change

result.summary: Wrote test/specs/REQ-052.md (7 ACs, each with concrete test-case rationale, not a restatement) and test/letflow/engine_cancel_instance_test.exs (new file, 9 tests across 7 describe blocks, mirroring engine_complete_task_test.exs's provisioned_tenant/0 + Sandbox :auto + async: false conventions, registering both TASK_COMPLETED and INSTANCE_CANCELLED event types). AC1: 2-open-task parallel-split cancel, verified by re-reading tasks/tokens/instance_projections/events. AC2: 3 tests -- already-CANCELLED conflict, already-COMPLETED conflict, and an ACTIVE zero-open-tasks instance (forced via direct Repo.update! bypassing complete_task/3, per INV-EE52-4) still appending one event. AC3: a real EventStore.append/2 call after cancellation returns {:error, {:instance_terminated, :cancelled}} against the real store. AC4: cancel_instance/3 vs complete_task/3 raced via Task.async/await_many (real concurrent Postgres connections, Sandbox :auto, not sequential calls), asserting exactly one winner and the correct one of the two distinct conflict tuples, cross-checked against final persisted state. AC5: compares Transition.transition/3's own pure :cancel_join outcome (JoinCounter with one outstanding branch, zero received) against a real cancel_instance/3 call's persisted instance_projections.status, both asserted == :cancelled and to each other explicitly. AC6/AC7: moduledoc content assertions via Code.fetch_docs/1 (SCH-03/S6/REQ-056 named as undone; ParallelApproval/ApprovalSupervisor deletion stated with the REQ-046 contrast reason) plus AC7's own Code.ensure_loaded/1 == {:error, :nofile} check that both modules are genuinely gone, not merely claimed deleted in prose. Every describe+test name combination checked programmatically, max observed ~169 chars, comfortably under the 200-char guidance and ExUnit's 255-char hard cap. mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors: clean, zero warnings. Ran mix test test/letflow/engine_cancel_instance_test.exs informally (not as a gate -- TEST-RUNNER owns that): 9 tests, 0 failures.
